subject: maths
title: Year 3 Fractions
seo_title: Year 3 Fractions Worksheets: Unit Fractions, Fractions of a Collection and Making a Whole (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Recognise and represent unit fractions including 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/5 and 1/10 and their multiples in different ways; combine fractions with the same denominator to complete the whole
meta_desc: Free Year 3 fractions worksheets for the Australian Curriculum: unit fractions of shapes, multiples like 3/5 and 7/10, fractions of a collection, number lines, making a whole and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, great NAPLAN practice.
key_big: The denominator is how many equal parts make the whole. The numerator is how many parts you have.
key_sub: 1/5 of 20: share 20 into 5 equal groups, and one group is 4. Fractions with the same denominator join to make a whole: 3/5 + 2/5 = 1.
body_html:
Unit fractions

A fraction is part of a whole. The whole must be split into equal parts.

A unit fraction is one equal part. It has 1 on top: 12, 13, 14, 15 and 110.

Multiples of unit fractions

PartWhat it tells youIn 34
Denominator (bottom number)How many equal parts make the whole4 equal parts
Numerator (top number)How many of those parts you have3 parts

34 is 3 lots of 14: 14 + 14 + 14 = 34.

Fractions of a collection

To find 15 of a collection, share it into 5 equal groups and count one group.

Example

What is 310 of 20?

20 ÷ 10 = 2, so one tenth is 2. Three tenths: 3 × 2 = 6.

Answer: 6

Fractions on a number line

Fractions are numbers between 0 and 1. Split 0 to 1 into equal spaces and count the spaces, not the marks.

Making a whole

When the numerator and the denominator are the same, you have the whole: 55 = 1. Fractions with the same denominator join to make the whole. Add the top numbers only.

Example

710 + ? = 1

1 whole is 1010. 10 − 7 = 3.

Answer: 310

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking 110 is bigger than 15 because 10 is bigger than 5More parts means smaller parts, so 110 < 15
Counting the parts that are not shadedThe numerator counts the shaded parts
Saying 15 of 20 is 55 is the number of groups. Count one group: 20 ÷ 5 = 4
Calling unequal parts “thirds” or “quarters”Fractions need equal parts
Adding the bottom numbers: 14 + 34 = 48The parts stay quarters: 44 = 1
Counting the marks on a number lineCount the spaces between the marks

faq.q: What fractions do Year 3 students learn in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: In Year 3 (AC9M3N02) students work with halves, thirds, quarters, fifths and tenths. They show unit fractions such as 1/5 and their multiples such as 3/5 with shapes, collections and number lines, and join fractions with the same denominator to make one whole.

faq.q: How do you find a fraction of a collection?
faq.a: Share the collection into as many equal groups as the denominator, then count the number of groups in the numerator. For 1/5 of 20, make 5 groups of 4, so the answer is 4.
Cut two same-size bars into 3 parts and into 5 parts. Each third is bigger, because the whole is shared into fewer parts.

faq.q: Are fractions in the Year 3 NAPLAN numeracy test?
faq.a: Yes, simple fraction questions can appear in Year 3 NAPLAN numeracy, such as naming a shaded fraction or finding a fraction of a group. Practising with pictures, collections and number lines helps.

items.q: What fraction of the circle is shaded?
items.e: The circle has 2 equal parts, so the denominator (bottom number) is 2. 1 part is shaded, so the numerator (top number) is 1. The answer is 12.

items.q: What fraction of the rectangle is shaded?
items.e: The rectangle has 4 equal parts, so the denominator (bottom number) is 4. 1 part is shaded, so the numerator (top number) is 1. The answer is 14.

items.q: What fraction of the bar is shaded?
items.e: The bar has 3 equal parts, so the denominator (bottom number) is 3. 1 part is shaded, so the numerator (top number) is 1. The answer is 13.

items.q: What fraction of the bar is shaded?
items.e: The bar has 5 equal parts, so the denominator (bottom number) is 5. 1 part is shaded, so the numerator (top number) is 1. The answer is 15.

items.q: What fraction of the rectangle is shaded?
items.e: The rectangle has 10 equal parts, so the denominator (bottom number) is 10. 1 part is shaded, so the numerator (top number) is 1. The answer is 110.

items.q: What fraction of the circle is shaded?
items.e: The circle has 3 equal parts, so the denominator (bottom number) is 3. 1 part is shaded, so the numerator (top number) is 1. The answer is 13.

items.q: What fraction of the bar is shaded?
items.e: The bar has 4 equal parts, so the denominator (bottom number) is 4. 1 part is shaded, so the numerator (top number) is 1. The answer is 14.

items.q: What fraction of the bar is shaded?
items.e: The bar has 10 equal parts, so the denominator (bottom number) is 10. 1 part is shaded, so the numerator (top number) is 1. The answer is 110.

items.q: Which picture shows 13 shaded?
items.e: 13 needs 3 equal parts with 1 shaded. That is picture C. A has 3 parts, but they are not equal. B shows 14. D shows 23.

items.q: Which picture shows 14 shaded?
items.e: 14 needs 4 equal parts with 1 shaded. That is picture D. A has 5 parts, so it shows 15. B shows 34. C has 4 parts, but they are not equal.

items.q: Which picture shows 15 shaded?
items.e: 15 needs 5 equal parts with 1 shaded. That is picture B. A shows 25. C has 5 parts, but they are not equal. D has 4 parts, so it shows 14.

items.q: Which picture shows 110 shaded?
items.e: 110 needs 10 equal parts with 1 shaded. That is picture A. B has 10 parts, but they are not equal. C has 5 parts, so it shows 15. D shows 910.

items.q: Does the shaded part show 14 of the bar?
c: No. The parts are not equal.
items.e: A fraction needs equal parts. These 4 parts are different sizes, so the shaded part is not 14.

items.q: Does the shaded part show 15 of the bar?
c: No. The parts are not equal.
items.e: A fraction needs equal parts. All 5 parts are the same size, so the shaded part is 15.

items.q: Does the shaded part show 13 of the bar?
c: No. The parts are not equal.
items.e: A fraction needs equal parts. These 3 parts are different sizes, so the shaded part is not 13.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Which shaded part is bigger?
items.e: The top bar is split into 3 parts and the bottom bar into 5 parts. Fewer parts means bigger parts, so 13 is bigger than 15.

items.q: Which unit fraction is the largest?
items.e: A unit fraction has 1 on top. The smallest denominator means the whole is cut into the fewest parts, so each part is biggest. 12 is the largest.

items.q: Which unit fraction is the smallest?
items.e: 10 is the biggest denominator. A whole cut into 10 equal parts has the smallest parts, so 110 is the smallest. A bigger number on the bottom does not mean a bigger fraction.

items.q: A shape is split into 3 equal parts. What is each part called?
items.e: 3 equal parts are called thirds. Each part is one third, 13. Three thirds is the whole shape.

items.q: A shape is split into 10 equal parts. What is each part called?
items.e: 10 equal parts are called tenths. Each part is one tenth, 110.

items.q: What fraction of the circle is shaded?
items.e: There are 4 equal parts, so each part is 14. 3 parts are shaded, so the answer is 34 (3 lots of 14).

items.q: What fraction of the bar is shaded?
items.e: There are 5 equal parts, so each part is 15. 2 parts are shaded, so the answer is 25 (2 lots of 15).

items.q: What fraction of the rectangle is shaded?
items.e: There are 10 equal parts, so each part is 110. 7 parts are shaded, so the answer is 710 (7 lots of 110).

items.q: What fraction of the bar is shaded?
items.e: There are 3 equal parts, so each part is 13. 2 parts are shaded, so the answer is 23 (2 lots of 13).

items.q: What fraction of the circle is shaded?
items.e: There are 5 equal parts, so each part is 15. 4 parts are shaded, so the answer is 45 (4 lots of 15).

items.q: What fraction of the bar is shaded?
items.e: There are 10 equal parts, so each part is 110. 3 parts are shaded, so the answer is 310 (3 lots of 110).

items.q: What fraction of the rectangle is shaded?
items.e: There are 4 equal parts, so each part is 14. 2 parts are shaded, so the answer is 24 (2 lots of 14).

items.q: What fraction of the circle is shaded?
items.e: There are 10 equal parts, so each part is 110. 9 parts are shaded, so the answer is 910 (9 lots of 110).

items.q: What fraction of the bar is not shaded?
items.e: There are 5 equal parts. 2 are shaded, so 5 − 2 = 3 parts are not shaded. The answer is 35.

items.q: What fraction of the rectangle is not shaded?
items.e: There are 10 equal parts. 3 are shaded, so 10 − 3 = 7 parts are not shaded. The answer is 710.

items.q: What fraction of the circle is not shaded?
items.e: There are 4 equal parts. 1 is shaded, so 4 − 1 = 3 parts are not shaded. The answer is 34.

items.q: 15 + 15 + 15 = ?
items.e: Three lots of one fifth is 3 fifths, 35. The parts stay fifths, so the denominator stays 5. Do not add the bottom numbers.

items.q: 710 is the same as how many lots of 110?
items.e: 710 means 7 tenths: 7 lots of 110.

items.q:
Count in fifths. What is the missing fraction?
15, 25, ?, 45
items.e: The denominator stays 5. The numerator goes up in 1s: 1, 2, 3, 4. The missing fraction is 35.

items.q: Which picture shows 35 shaded?
items.e: 35 needs 5 equal parts with 3 shaded. That is picture C. A shows 25. B has 5 parts, but they are not equal. D has 10 parts, so it shows 310.

items.q: Which picture shows 710 shaded?
items.e: 710 needs 10 equal parts with 7 shaded. That is picture D. A shows 310. B shows 610. C has 10 parts, but they are not equal.

items.q: Which picture shows 23 shaded?
items.e: 23 needs 3 equal parts with 2 shaded. That is picture D. A has 3 parts, but they are not equal. B has 4 parts, so it shows 24. C shows 33, the whole bar.

items.q: Compare the fractions. Choose <, > or =.
c: 35 < 45
35 > 45
35 = 45
items.e: The denominators are the same, so the parts are the same size. Compare the numerators: 3 is less than 4, so 35 < 45.

items.q: Compare the fractions. Choose <, > or =.
c: 910 < 710
910 > 710
910 = 710
items.e: The denominators are the same, so the parts are the same size. Compare the numerators: 9 is more than 7, so 910 > 710.

items.q: Compare the fractions. Choose <, > or =.
c: 23 < 13
23 > 13
23 = 13
items.e: The denominators are the same, so the parts are the same size. Compare the numerators: 2 is more than 1, so 23 > 13.

sets.title: Fractions of a collection and on a number line

items.q: What fraction of the counters are red?
items.e: There are 5 counters altogether, so the denominator is 5. 1 is red, so the numerator is 1. The answer is 15.

items.q: What fraction of the counters are red?
items.e: There are 10 counters altogether, so the denominator is 10. 3 are red, so the numerator is 3. The answer is 310.

items.q: What fraction of the counters are red?
items.e: There are 4 counters altogether, so the denominator is 4. 3 are red, so the numerator is 3. The answer is 34.

items.q: The 12 counters are in 2 equal groups. What is 12 of 12?
items.e: Share 12 into 2 equal groups: 12 ÷ 2 = 6. One group is 12.

items.q: The 15 counters are in 3 equal groups. What is 13 of 15?
items.e: Share 15 into 3 equal groups: 15 ÷ 3 = 5. One group is 13.

items.q: The 12 counters are in 4 equal groups. What is 14 of 12?
items.e: Share 12 into 4 equal groups: 12 ÷ 4 = 3. One group is 14.

items.q: The 20 counters are in 5 equal groups. What is 15 of 20?
items.e: Share 20 into 5 equal groups: 20 ÷ 5 = 4. One group is 15.

items.q: The 20 counters are in 10 equal groups. What is 110 of 20?
items.e: Share 20 into 10 equal groups: 20 ÷ 10 = 2. One group is 110.

items.q: The 16 counters are in 4 equal groups. What is 34 of 16?
items.e: First find 14: 16 ÷ 4 = 4. You need 3 groups, not 1: 4 × 3 = 12.

items.q: The 15 counters are in 5 equal groups. What is 25 of 15?
items.e: First find 15: 15 ÷ 5 = 3. You need 2 groups, not 1: 3 × 2 = 6.

items.q: The 30 counters are in 10 equal groups. What is 710 of 30?
items.e: First find 110: 30 ÷ 10 = 3. You need 7 groups, not 1: 3 × 7 = 21.

items.q: What is 15 of 35?
items.e: Share 35 into 5 equal groups: 35 ÷ 5 = 7. One group is 15.

items.q: What is 110 of 50?
items.e: Share 50 into 10 equal groups: 50 ÷ 10 = 5. One group is 110.

items.q: What is 23 of 18?
items.e: First find 13: 18 ÷ 3 = 6. You need 2 groups, not 1: 6 × 2 = 12.

items.q: What fraction is at the red dot?
items.e: Count the spaces, not the marks. From 0 to 1 there are 4 equal spaces, so each space is 14. The dot is 3 spaces from 0, so it is at 34.

items.q: What fraction is at the red dot?
items.e: Count the spaces, not the marks. From 0 to 1 there are 5 equal spaces, so each space is 15. The dot is 2 spaces from 0, so it is at 25.

items.q: What fraction is at the red dot?
items.e: Count the spaces, not the marks. From 0 to 1 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 110. The dot is 7 spaces from 0, so it is at 710.

items.q: What fraction is at the red dot?
items.e: Count the spaces, not the marks. From 0 to 1 there are 3 equal spaces, so each space is 13. The dot is 1 space from 0, so it is at 13.

items.q: Which letter shows 410?
items.e: The line from 0 to 1 has 10 equal spaces, so each space is 110. Count 4 spaces from 0. That is letter C.

items.q: Which letter shows 610?
items.e: The line from 0 to 1 has 10 equal spaces, so each space is 110. Count 6 spaces from 0. That is letter A.

sets.title: Combine fractions to make a whole

items.q:
The bar is 1 whole. 35 is shaded.
35 + ? = 1
items.e: The whole has 5 fifths. 3 are shaded, so 5 − 3 = 2 fifths are missing. 35 + 25 = 55 = 1.

items.q:
The bar is 1 whole. 14 is shaded.
14 + ? = 1
items.e: The whole has 4 quarters. 1 is shaded, so 4 − 1 = 3 quarters are missing. 14 + 34 = 44 = 1.

items.q:
The bar is 1 whole. 23 is shaded.
23 + ? = 1
items.e: The whole has 3 thirds. 2 are shaded, so 3 − 2 = 1 third is missing. 23 + 13 = 33 = 1.

items.q:
The bar is 1 whole. 710 is shaded.
710 + ? = 1
items.e: The whole has 10 tenths. 7 are shaded, so 10 − 7 = 3 tenths are missing. 710 + 310 = 1010 = 1.

items.q:
The bar is 1 whole. 12 is shaded.
12 + ? = 1
items.e: The whole has 2 halves. 1 is shaded, so 2 − 1 = 1 half is missing. 12 + 12 = 22 = 1.

items.q:
The bar is 1 whole. 410 is shaded.
410 + ? = 1
items.e: The whole has 10 tenths. 4 are shaded, so 10 − 4 = 6 tenths are missing. 410 + 610 = 1010 = 1.

items.q: 14 + 14 + 14 + 14 = ?
items.e: 4 quarters make 1 whole: 44 = 1. Do not add the bottom numbers.

items.q: 13 + 13 + 13 = ?
items.e: 3 thirds make 1 whole: 33 = 1. The parts stay thirds.

items.q: How many fifths make 1 whole?
items.e: 1 whole split into fifths has 5 equal parts: 55 = 1.

items.q: How many tenths make 1 whole?
items.e: 1 whole split into tenths has 10 equal parts: 1010 = 1.

items.q: Which two fractions make 1 whole?
c: 25 + 25
25 + 35
25 + 55
25 + 45
items.e: The fractions must have the same denominator and the numerators must add to 5: 2 + 3 = 5. So 25 + 35 = 55 = 1.

items.q: Which two fractions make 1 whole?
c: 310 + 610
310 + 310
310 + 810
310 + 710
items.e: The fractions must have the same denominator and the numerators must add to 10: 3 + 7 = 10. So 310 + 710 = 1010 = 1.

items.q: Which two fractions make 1 whole?
c: 14 + 34
14 + 14
14 + 24
14 + 44
items.e: The fractions must have the same denominator and the numerators must add to 4: 1 + 3 = 4. So 14 + 34 = 44 = 1.

items.q: Which two fractions make 1 whole?
c: 13 + 33
13 + 23
13 + 24
13 + 13
items.e: The fractions must have the same denominator and the numerators must add to 3: 1 + 2 = 3. So 13 + 23 = 33 = 1.

items.q: 15 + 25 + ? = 1
items.e: 1 whole is 55. 1 + 2 = 3, and 5 − 3 = 2. So the missing fraction is 25.

items.q: 210 + 510 + ? = 1
items.e: 1 whole is 1010. 2 + 5 = 7, and 10 − 7 = 3. So the missing fraction is 310.

items.q: 14 + 14 + ? = 1
items.e: 1 whole is 44. 1 + 1 = 2, and 4 − 2 = 2. So the missing fraction is 24.

items.q: The bar is 1 whole. Which number sentence matches the bar?
c: 25 + 25 = 1
25 + 35 = 510
25 + 35 = 1
25 + 45 = 1
items.e: 2 parts are shaded and 3 are white. 25 + 35 = 55, which is 1 whole. Add the numerators only. The denominator stays 5.

items.q: The bar is 1 whole. Which number sentence matches the bar?
c: 610 + 610 = 1
610 + 410 = 1020
610 + 510 = 1
610 + 410 = 1
items.e: 6 parts are shaded and 4 are white. 610 + 410 = 1010, which is 1 whole. Add the numerators only. The denominator stays 10.

items.q: The bar is 1 whole. Which number sentence matches the bar?
c: 13 + 23 = 1
13 + 13 = 1
13 + 23 = 36
13 + 33 = 1
items.e: 1 part is shaded and 2 are white. 13 + 23 = 33, which is 1 whole. Add the numerators only. The denominator stays 3.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 4 equal slices. Matilda eats 1 slice. What fraction of the pizza does she eat?
items.e: The pizza has 4 equal slices, so the denominator is 4. Matilda eats 1, so the answer is 14.

items.q: A family pizza is cut into 10 equal slices. The family eats 7 slices. What fraction of the pizza is left?
items.e: 10 − 7 = 3 slices are left out of 10 equal slices. The answer is 310.

items.q: A block of chocolate has 20 equal squares. Lachlan eats 15 of the block. How many squares does he eat?
items.e: Share 20 into 5 equal groups: 20 ÷ 5 = 4 squares. One group is 15.

items.q: There are 30 students in a Year 3 class. 110 of them walk to school. How many students walk to school?
items.e: Share 30 into 10 equal groups: 30 ÷ 10 = 3 students. One group is 110.

items.q: There are 30 students in a class. 13 of them ride a bike to school. How many students ride a bike?
items.e: Share 30 into 3 equal groups: 30 ÷ 3 = 10 students. One group is 13.

items.q: Leo has 24 stickers. 34 of them are koala stickers. How many koala stickers does he have?
items.e: First find 14: 24 ÷ 4 = 6. You need 3 groups, not 1: 6 × 3 = 18 stickers.

items.q: The school sausage sizzle has 40 sausages. 110 of them are vegetarian. How many vegetarian sausages are there?
items.e: Share 40 into 10 equal groups: 40 ÷ 10 = 4 sausages. One group is 110.

items.q: Sienna has 12 strawberries for recess. She gives 13 of them to a friend. How many does she give away?
items.e: Share 12 into 3 equal groups: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 strawberries. One group is 13.

items.q: Harper eats 25 of a cake. Oliver eats the rest. What fraction of the cake does Oliver eat?
items.e: The whole cake is 55. 55 − 25 = 35, because 2 + 3 = 5.

items.q: A watermelon is cut into 4 equal pieces. Cooper and Ethan each eat 1 piece. What fraction of the watermelon is left?
items.e: They eat 2 pieces, 14 + 14 = 24. 4 − 2 = 2 pieces are left, so 24 is left.

items.q: A game of AFL footy has 4 quarters. The teams have played 3 quarters. What fraction of the game is left?
items.e: The game is 4 equal quarters. 4 − 3 = 1 quarter is left: 14. 34 + 14 = 1.

items.q: On a school excursion, the class walks 1 km to the park. They have walked 610 of the way. What fraction of the way is left?
items.e: The whole walk is 1010. 10 − 6 = 4, so 410 of the way is left.

items.q: Ruby’s garden bed has 5 equal parts. 2 parts have tomatoes and 1 part has carrots. The rest have lettuce. What fraction of the garden bed has lettuce?
items.e: Tomatoes and carrots use 2 + 1 = 3 parts. 5 − 3 = 2 parts have lettuce: 25.

items.q: A jar has 10 marbles. 4 are blue and the rest are green. What fraction of the marbles are green?
items.e: 10 − 4 = 6 green marbles out of 10, so 610 are green.

items.q: Isla eats 14 of a sandwich. Chloe eats 34 of the same sandwich. How much of the sandwich do they eat altogether?
items.e: 14 + 34 = 44, and 44 is 1 whole. They eat the whole sandwich. Do not add the bottom numbers.

items.q: William eats 13 of a pizza. Charlotte eats 15 of a pizza of the same size. Who eats more?
items.e: A pizza cut into 3 has bigger slices than a pizza cut into 5. 13 > 15, so William eats more.

items.q: Mia says 110 is bigger than 15 because 10 is bigger than 5. Is she right?
c: No, 15 is bigger
items.e: Cutting a whole into 10 parts makes smaller parts than cutting it into 5. So 15 > 110.

items.q: Liam cuts a cake into 3 pieces. The pieces are different sizes. He says each piece is 13 of the cake. Is he right?
c: No, it should be 14
Yes, each piece is one part
No, the pieces are not equal
items.e: Thirds must be 3 equal parts. The pieces are different sizes, so they are not thirds.

items.q: Grace cuts a ribbon into 5 equal pieces. What fraction of the ribbon is each piece?
items.e: The whole ribbon is shared into 5 equal pieces. Each piece is 15. (4 cuts make 5 pieces.)

items.q: There are 10 players at netball training. 25 of them are wearing a hat. How many are not wearing a hat?
items.e: 25 of 10: 10 ÷ 5 = 2, and 2 × 2 = 4 players wear a hat. 10 − 4 = 6 players do not. (That is 35 of 10.)
